.jl-hero { box-sizing:border-box; display:grid; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.5fr) minmax(220px,.8fr); gap:clamp(2rem,5vw,4rem); align-items:start; width:min(100% - 3rem,1100px); margin:0 auto; padding:clamp(3rem,6vw,5rem) 0; }

.jl-contact-circle { width:66px; height:66px; border:1.6px solid var(--petrol); border-radius:50%; display:grid; place-items:center; color:var(--petrol); font-family:Arial,sans-serif; font-size:1.55rem; font-weight:650; transition:background .15s,color .15s,border-color .15s; }
.jl-contact-links a:hover .jl-contact-circle { background:var(--coral); border-color:var(--coral); color:white; }

body:has(.jl-hero) #title-block-header, body:has(.jl-hero) header#title-block-header {display:none !important;}

}

    <h1 class="jl-name">Javier Lera</h1>
    <p class="jl-role">Assistant Professor of Economics</p>
    <div class="jl-accent-rule" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    <p class="jl-intro">I am an <strong>applied economist</strong> at the University of Cantabria (Spain). My research lies at the intersection of health economics, public economics and social policy, with a particular focus on socioeconomic inequalities, ageing, well-being and public policy evaluation.</p>
    <p class="jl-intro">I hold a PhD in Economics from an interuniversity doctoral programme involving the University of Cantabria, the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU) and the University of Oviedo. Before my current position, I worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the Valdecilla Biomedical Research Institute (IDIVAL). My work draws on applied microeconometric methods, and I have participated in national and European research projects.</p>
